builder_plan.scenario: Your coding assistant makes changes that still need substantial repair before merging.
builder_plan.change: Try the technique on held-out issues from a repository with reliable tests.
builder_plan.baseline: The same coding agent, repository snapshot, tools, and token budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct patches, regression failures, human repair time, and total cost per accepted change.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: System Optimizations for Cost-Efficient Agent Harnesses
summary: Replaces ad-hoc harness configurations with a unified interposition platform (Agency) that layers system optimizations onto existing agent harnesses without modifying the underlying model. Costs engineering effort to integrate the interposition layer and validate that optimizations preserve task accuracy on the specific workload. Optimizations derived from trace analysis may not transfer to tasks whose cost accumulation patterns differ from those studied, and the platform dependency introduces a maintenance burden.
rationale: The reader operates LLM agents via APIs under cost constraints, so a harness-level optimization that reduces token use and LLM calls without model changes is directly applicable, but the 35% figure requires validation on the reader's own task distribution before production adoption.
technique: Harness interposition for agent cost optimization

claims.statement: Replaces ad-hoc harness configurations with a unified interposition platform (Agency) that layers system optimizations onto existing agent harnesses without modifying the underlying model. Costs engineering effort to integrate the interposition layer and validate that optimizations preserve task accuracy on the specific workload. Optimizations derived from trace analysis may not transfer to tasks whose cost accumulation patterns differ from those studied, and the platform dependency introduces a maintenance burden.

Cost reductions up to 35% across real-world benchmarks on existing harnesses such as Claude Code and OpenAI Codex, without compromising accuracy; harness-side variances show cost reductions up to 2.6x on the same model and task.
